description: Stress arising from a sense that the cat's home range or personal space is unclear or contested.
Active patrol or defense behavior at thresholds, doorways, or the edges of claimed territory.
Heightened watchfulness and scanning behavior, often from a high vantage point.
Distress from an excess of social contact — too many people, too much handling, too much noise at once.
Distress specifically tied to separation from, or anticipation of separation from, a bonded human.
Active proximity-seeking and shadowing of a specific bonded human.
Stress arising from an unpredictable or recently-changed daily schedule (feeding, sleep, human presence).
Broken, shortened, or erratic sleep bouts rather than the cat's typical long stretches.
Elevated activity specifically during night hours, out of proportion to daytime activity.
Strong, repeated attachment to one specific object, texture, or item used as a coping anchor.
Possessive or defensive behavior around food, water, or litter access points.
Friction, avoidance, or vigilance arising specifically from cohabitation with other cats.
Increased frequency, volume, or insistence of vocalization beyond the cat's own baseline.
Unusually reduced vocalization — an atypical quietness read as withdrawal rather than contentment.
Grooming behavior that exceeds routine self-maintenance, used as self-soothing under stress.
Signs of under-stimulation arising from insufficient active play or environmental engagement.
Active interest in new objects, textures, or environmental changes — the drive an under-stimulated cat is trying to satisfy.
